Welcome. This site collects everything you need for the course: the lecture
recordings, student lecture notes, the homework problem set, and the solutions
that exist for it.

**Instructor:** [Prof. Andy Ruina](https://ruina.org) · taught at Plaksha
University using the Cornell lecture recordings.

```{python}
#| echo: false
#| output: asis
import sys
sys.path.insert(0, "scripts")
import coursesite as S

meta = S.load("meta")
c = meta["counts"]
bits = [f"**{c['lectures']}** lectures", f"**{c['homeworks']}** homework problems"]
if meta["notes_sets"]:
    bits.append(f"**{len(meta['notes_sets'])}** sets of lecture notes")
print(" · ".join(bits))
```

## Getting started

1. Read the [Course Outline](outline.qmd) — in particular the grading split.
2. Skim the [homework policy](homework.qmd#homework-policy) before your first
   submission.
3. Work through the [Lectures](lectures.qmd) at roughly two per week, doing the
   matching homework as you go.

::: {.callout-tip}
Solutions marked ⚠ have not been reviewed by the instructor. Treat them as a
hint or a cross-check, not as a model answer.
:::
